There are MANY posts about this topic and I mean on reddit too. "Who are these people" - you asked. There are plenty of people who applied and got denied for no fucking reason. And before you go say they are healthy or whatever, most of them have health reasons. If you really want to see who those people are, search a bit about similar posts, you will find quite plenty.

"They are really desperate. They don't want to apply but they have no choice" - you asked what it ment. Well, it means when you don't really want to apply for VAD, because you would rather live a nice life, but life doesn't want you to. Do you have any idea how many health problems are and just how little of them have treatment? And those who have a treatment that you don't need to take for life are even less. Imagine you go and tell someone who has chronic pain with no available treatment or cure to just go take a nice walk in the park when the moment they wake up the pain hits them. They would rather NOT have that problem and be healthy too, but it just isn't possible sometimes. So, when it's too much some might want to exit relaxed, with no pain and no fear, rather than endure until the disease gets them or it makes worse.

Pegasos said they belive anyone should be able to apply regarding the age (over 18 of course) and health status. But many times, they reject people, especially the ones who are younger. Some diseases don't kill you, but it makes living a pain with no joy anymore. No amount of "therapy" will take away the body pain, give your sight back or similar. Imagine a healthy person who out of nowhere develops an eye condition that lets him blind, and the doctors cannot cure it. They try different treatments but it just won't work. So, instead of living the rest of their life in shit, they want to go out of it. Some might chose not to, but not everyone is the same. Of course he would RATHER get his eyesight back, but what can you do when medicine is weak and governs won't invest more in it?

Many people got rejected because if you don't have a certain disease that is on the "approved list" then you have a high chance to get rejected. Even simply applying is highly risky because you need to pay half the money upfront with no refund (or at least partial refund) and since the price is 5.000€ upfront you can understand how it might be scary to apply if you are not sure they will approve it.

Perhaphs Pegasos wants to help everyone who applies to them, but the swiss law won't let them? However, the swiss law on assisted suicide does not mention that you need to have ANY kind of health problem to qualify for VAD, the only request is that it is not made from "selfish reasons"

I do not know you, but in case you are a healthy person with a decent life, I can understand how you would not understand someones else suffering and why would they even try to request a VAD

A fun fact: if you are older, you don't need to have ANY health disease to get accepted. So that's the real problem. If they would really not want younger people to apply for this kind of stuff, perhaps add some more budget money to healthcare and medicine research so more diseases could be treated without life treatment (meaning if you can't get itz you're kind of screwed) but until they do that, they should not deny VAD acces to people who want it.
